title: Container-aware Kanban column sizing is wired to ONE call site — the swimlane layout never reads it and still paints the hard-coded `w-[85vw]` its own docblock says was replaced
body:
Filed by the `domain:ui` PM seat (`session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S`). Measured on `origin/main`. ⛔ Not claimed.

## The claim the code makes

`packages/plugin-kanban/src/KanbanImpl.tsx:401-405`:

> *"Container-aware column sizing — **replaces hard-coded `w-[85vw] sm:w-80`** (viewport-relative) with a width derived from the board's own slot. That way an embedded Kanban (in a panel, drawer, or pop-out window) scales correctly without overflowing or wasting space."*

## What is actually wired

`columnInlineStyle` (computed at `:408`) is consumed at **exactly one** call site in the repository:

```
:655   {swimlanes ? (                      ← swimlane branch begins
:687     header cells   w-[85vw] sm:w-80   hard-coded
:721     lane cells     w-[85vw] sm:w-80   hard-coded
:738   ) : (                               ← non-swimlane branch begins
:751     columnStyle={columnInlineStyle}   ← the ONLY consumer
```

The mechanism itself is correct where it is reached — `KanbanColumn` at `:289-293` does the two-way switch properly (`columnStyle.width != null ? "shrink-0" : "w-[85vw] sm:w-80 shrink-0"`, so the viewport classes step aside rather than fight the inline width).

The swimlane branch simply never reaches it. Its own docblock at `:661-664` explains why the wiring is not a one-liner:

> *"this layout has no column components at all — every lane paints its own row of plain column cells"*

So an **embedded swimlane board — a panel, a drawer, a pop-out window, exactly the case the feature was built for — is still sized to the viewport.** The sentence "replaces hard-coded `w-[85vw] sm:w-80`" is true of one of the two layouts.

## ⚠️ Correction to an earlier reading of this, recorded so it is not repeated

An earlier pass by this seat reported the defect as a *misalignment between the swimlane header row and its columns*. **That was wrong** and the table it produced should be ignored. The swimlane layout has no `KanbanColumnView` at all; its header cells (`:687`) and lane cells (`:721`) carry the identical hard-coded class, so they agree with each other. The defect is that the whole swimlane layout is viewport-sized, not that its parts disagree.

The mistake came from reading `:687`/`:721` without locating the ternary boundary at `:738`. Whoever takes this should confirm the boundary first.

## Instrument — this one CAN go in CI

The width here is a **prop / inline style**, not a layout result, so it is readable without measuring pixels. Pin *"the swimlane header cell and lane cell receive their width from the same source as a non-swimlane column does"* rather than any rendered dimension.

That sidesteps the problem `swimlaneColumnHeaderRow-7303.test.tsx` documents at length: the `:665-681` docblock records that the original defect could only be caught in a real Chromium at 1600x1000 (row height 0, `elementFromPoint` returning the collapse button behind the title). **Do not try to re-measure heights in jsdom.**

`useResizeObserver` yields no width in jsdom, so decide deliberately how the fixture supplies a board width — and note that a fixture with **no** width exercises the `if (!boardWidth) return {}` early-out, which is a third state, not a stand-in for either.

## ⭐ Non-regression axis

The caricature is deleting the viewport classes outright, leaving swimlane cells with no width at all. It would pass any "the swimlane cell no longer carries `w-[85vw]`" assertion. Pin positively that a swimlane cell gets a real width from the container-derived source at each of the three `columnInlineStyle` tiers (`< 480` → `boardWidth - 32` floored at 220, `< 720` → 280, else 320), and that the non-swimlane layout is unchanged.

## Related

objectui#7303 (the swimlane column-header row, where this code was last touched) · objectui#4254 (Kanban drop validation, closed — unrelated mechanism, same file)

## Dedup

Ran, single-token `search_issues`. `swimlane` returns **0**, and the lit control for the same query shape is `KanbanImpl` → 1 hit (objectui#4254, closed, `requiredWhen` on drop — a different mechanism). So the zero is a real absence in a reachable index, not a dead instrument. Nothing filed about Kanban column sizing.
